feature.name: Find Clinical Trials
feature.description: Find recruiting clinical trials by condition. Decomposed into three stories (data retrieval, display, architecture). Stories and requirements pending operator approval of V5 draft in _oneshots/EPIC-006-F-031_FindClinicalTrials_FeatureDraft_V5.docx.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials data retrieval
story.description: ClinicalTrialsTool data-retrieval contract: CT.gov v2 search parameters, the geographic_scope filter (international or US-only), pagination defaults, demographic filters (age, sex), the canonical search_context echo, and the deterministic /gate op for pagination.

requirement.name: Request totalCount from CT.gov and surface the total to callers
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST send countTotal=true on every CT.gov v2 /studies request and parse payload.totalCount from the response. The total MUST be surfaced on Response.total_count for downstream display. CT.gov returns totalCount as an integer when countTotal=true.

requirement.name: Default page size of 10 records
requirement.requirement: Request.page_size MUST default to 10 (down from 25). The user explicitly paginates with the cursor returned in Response.cursor; the wrapper's pagination control mirrors the providers pagination pattern.

requirement.name: Accept optional participant demographics (age, sex)
requirement.requirement: Request MUST accept two optional participant-demographic fields: age_years (Optional[int]) and sex (Optional[str]). Condition remains the only required field. When age_years is supplied, ClinicalTrialsTool MUST map to CT.gov aggFilters using the canonical buckets: age<18 -> ages:child, 18<=age<65 -> ages:adult, age>=65 -> ages:older. When sex is supplied, ClinicalTrialsTool MUST resolve it to 'm' or 'f' (per S-003-REQ-B-007) and map to CT.gov sex:m or sex:f. Gender is intentionally NOT a parameter on this tool -- sex alone drives the CT.gov filter.

requirement.name: Always emit a 'trials' stream event on every code path
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST emit a {kind:'trials', data:Response} stream event on every code path -- success, empty result set, error. The client relies on the trials event as the canonical end-of-search signal; silent paths previously caused 'no trials event in stream' user-visible failures.

requirement.name: Echo authoritative SearchContext on every Response
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST populate Response.search_context with the exact {condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope} actually used to fetch this page. The client uses search_context to re-issue pagination requests against the same canonical criteria, preventing the raw user utterance from leaking into the CT.gov call on subsequent pages.

requirement.name: Routes API failures must be surfaced (no silent swallow)
requirement.requirement: When the Google Routes API call for a destination fails, the tool MUST log the failure as a Mode 2 ChatHealthyException in one of four named modes: routes_api_key_missing (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY env var absent), routes_api_non_200 (HTTP response not 200), routes_api_empty (200 with empty routes[]), and routes_api_failed (exception during the call). Distance/duration MAY remain absent on the affected Location; the operator is notified via the log.

requirement.name: Direct deterministic pagination op on /gate
requirement.requirement: SharedServices /gate MUST accept op='clinical_trials_page' with a payload matching ClinicalTrialsTool.Request (condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope, cursor, page_size). UR dispatches to ClinicalTrialsTool with no LLM and no UtteranceManager hop. This is the deterministic path the client uses for More / Back pagination clicks (REQ-B-068).

requirement.name: Geographic scope: international (default) or US-only
requirement.requirement: Request MUST accept an optional geographic_scope field with values 'international' (default) or 'us'. ClinicalTrialsTool MUST honor it as follows: 'international' applies NO geographic filter to CT.gov (all records returned worldwide). 'us' MUST add the CT.gov v2 GEO filter restricting to country=United States. No other per-country scoping is supported in this iteration -- the only choices are international or US.

requirement.name: Unit tests cover every public component of ClinicalTrialsTool
requirement.requirement: Every public method/function of ClinicalTrialsTool -- including but not limited to: CT.gov request builder, response parser, age_years -> aggFilter mapper, sex -> aggFilter mapper, geographic_scope -> GEO filter mapper, brief_summary first-sentence truncator, search_context echo populator, Routes API caller -- MUST have unit tests. Each component's test set MUST include at least ONE positive case (asserting the happy-path output) AND at least ONE anticipated negative case (e.g. missing input, malformed input, upstream failure mode, boundary condition). Tests live in FindCare/ClinicalTrials/tests/ alongside the tool source. No test may share state with another test.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials display
story.description: Front-end display contract: left-panel header band, first-sentence truncation, More/Back pagination, center-panel section anchors, right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll, loading banner content and timer behavior, intent_classified mid-stream banner update, and the pagination error overlay verb context.

requirement.name: Left-panel brief_summary truncated to first sentence with ellipsis
requirement.requirement: In the per-trial card in the left panel, the trial's brief_summary MUST be displayed truncated to its first sentence. When truncation occurs (the first sentence is shorter than the full summary), '...' MUST be appended to signal truncation. The user clicks the trial's NCT id to view the full detail in the main window.

requirement.name: Left-panel header band: canonical query criteria + record range
requirement.requirement: The colored header band at the top of the left panel MUST display the canonical query criteria as echoed by the tool (Response.search_context). Format: 'Clinical trials -- condition: <X>, subject age: <Y>, subject sex: <Z>, <location>, scope: <international|US>'. When the tool returns a total_count, the band MUST also append ' -- showing <start> to <end> of <total>'. When total is unknown the band MUST NOT show a count (it MUST NOT imply a count it does not know).

requirement.name: Left-panel More / Back pagination controls
requirement.requirement: The left panel MUST render a 'more trials' link when Response.cursor is non-null and a 'back' link when prior cursors exist (client-side history). Clicking either MUST round-trip through ClientRouter.getStreamedPayloads to /gate op='clinical_trials_page' (REQ-B-073) -- NOT through the LLM-routed utterance path. The pagination control mirrors the providers pagination pattern.

requirement.name: Center-panel trial detail: section anchors
requirement.requirement: Every section in the main-window trial detail MUST carry a stable anchor id of the form id="ct-sec-<slug>" where <slug> is a lowercased hyphenated form of the section title. The anchors are the targets for right-panel section-list jump links (REQ-B-070).

requirement.name: Right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll jumps
requirement.requirement: When a trial is displayed in the main window, the right panel MUST render a 'Trial sections' list with one clickable link per section in the current trial (linked to the anchor ids from REQ-B-069). Clicking a link MUST smooth-scroll the main-window center to that section's anchor.

requirement.name: Immediate clear + timer on More / Back click
requirement.requirement: When the user clicks More or Back in the left panel, the system MUST immediately (before the network round-trip): clear the main-window trial detail, clear the right-panel section list, start a one-second-tick timer from zero, and render a loading banner. Then the network fetch is issued. The user must never see stale data while a new page is being fetched.

requirement.name: Loading banner content: canonical criteria + record range
requirement.requirement: The loading banner MUST display the canonical criteria (REQ-B-067 format, INCLUDING the geographic_scope) plus the record range being retrieved, e.g. 'condition: hepatitis B, subject age: 28, subject sex: male, Los Angeles, scope: US -- retrieving records 11-20 of 247'. The banner MUST NOT show only the raw user verb. The timer ticks every second next to or under the banner.

requirement.name: Mid-stream loading-banner update from intent_classified
requirement.requirement: On a fresh utterance flow, when UR has finished classifying the utterance into a findClinicalTrials intent, UR MUST emit a {kind:'intent_classified'} stream event carrying the canonical criteria (action, condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope). The client MUST replace the loading banner's raw utterance text with the canonical criteria as soon as that event arrives, so the user sees what the system actually understood, not the raw utterance.

requirement.name: Pagination error overlay must include verb context
requirement.requirement: When a More / Back pagination fetch fails, the client error overlay MUST prepend a verb-context clause to the underlying error message: 'While trying to load more clinical trials: <err>' (for next) or 'While trying to go back to the previous page of clinical trials: <err>' (for prev). The user must always see what action was in flight when the error occurred.

requirement.name: Standalone Playwright test for the clinical-trials display
requirement.requirement: A NEW Playwright test MUST be created at architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/find_care_clinical_trials_test.py covering every display REQ in Story S-002 -- at minimum: the left-panel header band format, the first-sentence truncation with ellipsis, the More / Back pagination controls and their round-trip through op='clinical_trials_page', the center-panel section anchors, the right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll, the immediate clear+timer on click, the loading-banner content and intent_classified update, and the pagination-error overlay verb context. The test MUST be INDEPENDENT of the smoke Playwright test -- the smoke only confirms the page renders and each iframe shows good content at a high level; this test asserts the fine-grained display contract. The test MUST fetch a real clinical trial from clinicaltrials.gov v2 (a stable, recruiting NCT id with a known section structure) as the reference fixture and assert against its actual data. The test MUST allow parameterized exercise of different search parameters (condition, age, sex, location, scope) and full pagination cycles (More, Back, More, etc.). If an existing Playwright test already covers any of this surface, that test is reused (and extended where it is incomplete) rather than duplicated.

requirement.name: Selected trial highlighted in left panel; click clears center+right immediately, then paints new trial
requirement.requirement: In the left-panel trial list, the trial currently displayed in frame_MainWindow MUST be visually distinguished (highlighted background) so the user always knows which card they are viewing. When the user clicks any trial card, the system MUST IMMEDIATELY blank frame_MainWindow and frame_RightPanel (paint empty content) BEFORE painting the new trial, so the user has an unambiguous visual confirmation that the click registered even when the new trial is fetched from the same in-memory page (no backend hop). The new trial's full detail is then painted into frame_MainWindow and its section-list into frame_RightPanel, and the left-panel highlight moves to the newly-selected card.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials architecture
story.description: Architecture contract between UtteranceManager, Universal Router, and ClinicalTrialsTool. UM prompts for refinements on first turn and extracts on follow-up; LLM (not regex) resolves the sex answer; condition is the only required field; UR thin pass-through for the deterministic pagination op.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager prompts for refinements on first clinical-trial turn
requirement.requirement: On the FIRST turn where the user expresses clinical-trial interest, UM MUST set target_action='closeConnection200' and emit a user_message that names EVERY refinement field not already known. The literal words 'age', 'sex', 'location', and 'scope' (asking international vs US) MUST appear in the user_message for each field that is missing. UM MUST tell the user that condition alone is enough -- they can answer 'skip' for any field. Park a pending_disambiguation with kind='clinical_trial_demographics'. UM MAY skip the ask and dispatch findClinicalTrials directly ONLY when all refinements are already known.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager extracts age_years, sex, user_location, geographic_scope from follow-up
requirement.requirement: On the FOLLOW-UP turn after the prompt, UM MUST extract every refinement supplied. age_years (int) from 'I'm 28' / '28' / '28yo' / 'age 28'. sex (lowercased 'm' or 'f') per REQ-B-007. user_location (free-text) from any location mention. geographic_scope ('international' or 'us') from any 'international'/'worldwide'/'US only'/'United States only' mention. Populate all extracted fields as Arguments on the findClinicalTrials intent. If the user declines ('skip', 'no', 'just show me'), proceed with whatever fields are populated. Always set target_action='findClinicalTrials'.

requirement.name: LLM-driven resolution of the user's sex answer to 'm' or 'f'
requirement.requirement: UM MUST resolve the user's answer to the sex prompt — or any sex signal in a free-text utterance — into the canonical lowercase token 'm' or 'f' via the classifier LLM. The LLM, not regex, MUST be authoritative. The LLM MUST recognize: (a) direct labels — 'Male', 'M', 'man', 'boy', 'masculino' → 'm'; 'Female', 'F', 'woman', 'girl' → 'f'; (b) male family / relationship words referring to the subject — 'son', 'brother', 'father', 'dad', 'uncle', 'nephew', 'grandfather', 'grandpa', 'husband', 'boyfriend', 'fiancé' → 'm'; (c) female family / relationship words — 'daughter', 'sister', 'mother', 'mom', 'aunt', 'niece', 'grandmother', 'grandma', 'wife', 'girlfriend', 'fiancée' → 'f'; (d) third-person pronouns about the subject when no contradicting label is present — 'he', 'his', 'him' → 'm'; 'she', 'her', 'hers' → 'f'. If the answer is ambiguous, non-binary, or mixes signals the LLM cannot reconcile, sex MUST be left None and the search dispatches without a sex filter. Gender is not a parameter in this iteration; we ask sex only. The same rules apply BOTH on the dedicated follow-up prompt AND on the first turn when the user volunteers the information ('clinical trial for my son who is 9' → sex='m', age_years=9).

requirement.name: Condition is the ONLY required field for findClinicalTrials
requirement.requirement: Across the entire clinical-trials flow (UM extraction, UR dispatch, tool execution), condition is the ONLY required field. age_years, sex, user_location, and geographic_scope are ALL optional refinements of equal stature -- none is 'primary', none is 'bonus'. The search MUST dispatch with whatever the user provides, including no refinements at all if the user skips every field. Default scope when omitted is 'international' (REQ-B-074).

requirement.name: Universal Router dispatches /gate op=clinical_trials_page as a thin pass-through
requirement.requirement: When /gate receives op='clinical_trials_page', UR MUST invoke _handle_clinical_trials_page which constructs a clinical_trials_tool.Request from the payload (Pydantic validates) and calls TOOL.run_and_log(deps, request). No biz logic in the handler -- all biz logic lives in ClinicalTrialsTool. UR also emits {kind:'intent_classified'} per REQ-B-073 on the LLM-routed findClinicalTrials dispatch path so the client can update its loading banner.

requirement.name: Unit tests cover UtteranceManager clinical-trial extraction paths
requirement.requirement: Every UM extraction rule in S-003 -- first-turn prompt construction (REQ-B-005), follow-up extraction of age / sex / location / scope (REQ-B-006), LLM-driven sex resolution (REQ-B-007), and the condition-only required-field guarantee (REQ-B-008) -- MUST have unit tests. Each rule's test set MUST include at least ONE positive case (e.g. user supplies all refinements; UM extracts cleanly) AND at least ONE anticipated negative case (e.g. user says 'skip'; ambiguous sex answer the LLM cannot resolve; user supplies an unsupported country for geographic_scope and UM falls back to international). Tests live alongside the UM source.

feature.name: FindCareRequestManager
feature.description: This feature specifies how FindCare uses the ManageRequests functions to send requests to peer services and to handle requests received from them. Its four stories cover synchronous send, synchronous receive, asynchronous send, and asynchronous receive.

story.name: FindCare Make Synchronous Request
story.description: FindCare, on a user thread, initiates a synchronous call to a peer service and waits for the response before continuing.

requirement.name: FindCare makes synchronous requests
requirement.requirement: FindCare, on a user thread, MUST be able to initiate a synchronous call to a peer service and wait for the peer's response before continuing its own work.

requirement.name: FindCare synchronous outbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every synchronous outbound request MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that FindCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the current User State as a first-class field. The returned response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by the peer.

story.name: FindCare Receive Synchronous Request
story.description: FindCare, on a user thread, satisfies a synchronous request from a peer and returns the result before the peer continues its own work.

requirement.name: FindCare satisfies synchronous requests
requirement.requirement: FindCare, on a user thread, MUST be able to satisfy a synchronous request from a peer and return the result before the peer continues its own work.

requirement.name: FindCare synchronous inbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every synchronous inbound request handler MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that FindCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the caller's current User State as a first-class field. The returned response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by FindCare.

story.name: FindCare Make Asynchronous Request
story.description: FindCare initiates an asynchronous call to a peer service and continues without waiting; the response is delivered later via a callback FindCare supplies.

requirement.name: FindCare makes asynchronous requests
requirement.requirement: FindCare MUST be able to initiate an asynchronous call to a peer service and continue its own work without waiting for the peer's response.

requirement.name: FindCare asynchronous outbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every asynchronous outbound request MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that FindCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the current User State as a first-class field. The delivered response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by the peer.

requirement.name: FindCare asynchronous outbound supplies a callback mechanism
requirement.requirement: Every asynchronous outbound request MUST supply a callback mechanism through which the peer's response is delivered. The callback mechanism MUST be an API endpoint, an in-memory event, or both.

story.name: FindCare Receive Asynchronous Request
story.description: FindCare accepts an asynchronous request, allows the peer to continue, and later delivers the response via the caller-supplied callback.

requirement.name: FindCare accepts asynchronous requests
requirement.requirement: FindCare MUST be able to accept an asynchronous request from a peer and produce the response after the caller has continued its own work.

requirement.name: FindCare asynchronous inbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every asynchronous inbound request handler MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that FindCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the caller's current User State as a first-class field. The delivered response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by FindCare.

requirement.name: FindCare asynchronous inbound delivers via caller's callback mechanism
requirement.requirement: The response MUST be delivered to the caller through the callback mechanism the caller supplied in the original request. The callback mechanism MUST be an API endpoint, an in-memory event, or both.

Baseline rules that MUST be observed in the reactive interface: (a) every interactive control presents a minimum 44x44pt hit target (HIG Inputs); (b) layouts honor safe-area insets via CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) with the document declaring <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"> so content clears the Dynamic Island and home indicator (HIG Layout); (c) text contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large) as cross-referenced by HIG Accessibility; (d) body type sizes use rem so they honor user Dynamic Type / browser zoom settings; (e) primary actions on phone breakpoints (<= 600px) sit within the lower-third thumb zone of the viewport. The version of HIG in force is the current published edition; the citation MUST be re-pinned if Apple issues a major guide revision.
requirement.name: Technical requirement MUST cite the exact best-practice phone/iPad style guide in use

feature.name: Engineering Rule Enforcement
feature.description:
This feature specifies the rules that must be enforced by the chatHealthy.ai dev ops infrastructure utilizing the Anthopic Hooks as event triggers. 
It specifies the concrete DevOps surface that wires Claude Code's hook architecture into ChatHealthy governance. Hosts SessionStart / PostCompact / UserPromptSubmit / Stop enforcement entries declared in engineering_rules.json, the chathealthy_devops_boot program (Rule-002), and the conversation-log persistence path (Rule-001). Owns the operator-visible boot lifecycle: conversation context replay and agile_backlog taxonomy injection on both new-session begin and post-compaction restart.

story.name: Rules infrastructure: manager, base worker, lock, timeout, telemetry, exit-code aggregation
story.description: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager + EnforcementWorker (abstract base) deliver the framework: read-only rules-registry load, hook-filtered enforcement dispatch, manager-owned mutex coordination, per-worker subprocess timeout, structured violation/telemetry envelopes, and worst-code-wins aggregation. Per V20 Â§4.4. The manager is invoked by every Git and Claude Code hook with a single hook_name argument.

requirement.name: Rules carry enforcement entries
requirement.requirement: Every engineering rule that the team intends to enforce MUST carry at least one programmatic enforcement entry. A rule with an empty enforcement array is documentation, not governance, and SHALL be either populated, retired, or annotated as documentation-only.

requirement.name: Enforcement at hook moment
requirement.requirement: Enforcement runs at the moment a violation can occur â€” the relevant Git or Claude Code hook â€” not on a separate cadence. There is no nightly job that catches yesterday's mistake.

requirement.name: Hook-agnostic framework
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule MUST be able to attach to any of the four Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push) and any of the six Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded). The framework is hook-agnostic; the enforcement entry declares its hook.

requirement.name: Human debuggability
requirement.requirement: The system MUST be debuggable by a human. One file per role. One class per file. One entry point. Per-enforcement, per-worker structured stdout and telemetry, with worst exit code propagated.

requirement.name: Multi-PID concurrency
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST handle multi-PID race conditions correctly. The same hook can fire many times concurrently across different Claude Code PIDs and Git invocations. The manager acquires a lock before dispatching any worker whose enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True; in-process locks are forbidden.

requirement.name: Additive enforcement
requirement.requirement: Adding the next enforcement MUST be a small, additive change. New enforcement entries get a new enforcement_id and â€” if needed â€” a new worker subclass; existing rules and workers are not touched.

requirement.name: Worker inherits base class
requirement.requirement: Every worker MUST inherit from EnforcementWorker. Subclasses implement only their domain-specific check logic. The base class owns scope evaluation, violation shape, exit codes, telemetry, and error handling so every worker behaves the same from the manager's perspective.

requirement.name: Enforcement entry first-class
requirement.requirement: Enforcement entries are first-class records: every entry carries a stable enforcement_id (format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN), a declared hook, an executable_path, a scopes field carrying scope-list rules in the four canonical types (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern), and a requires_lock boolean. They can be cited in audit trails, bug reports, and the backlog like requirements are today.

requirement.name: Filesystem mirrors operating model
requirement.requirement: The architecture MUST be aligned with the EPIC / Feature / Story tree. Filesystem mirrors operating model. The home for this feature is projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/. crossEpicConcerns/ holds shared business artifacts only â€” no code lives there.

requirement.name: V1 demonstrability
requirement.requirement: Once V1 ships, BR-1 through BR-9 are demonstrably satisfied for the worked example (file scanning on pre-commit) and the framework is in place to absorb every other rule on its own schedule.

requirement.name: Four canonical scope-list types
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST support all four scope-list types on every enforcement entry, even when a given worker uses only a subset. The four permitted terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) are the only vocabulary used anywhere in this system.

requirement.name: Enforcement schema fields
requirement.requirement: engineering_rules.json schema gains the following required fields per enforcement entry: enforcement_id (string, format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN); hook (enum: pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded); executable_path (string â€” repo-relative path to the worker script that implements this enforcement); requires_lock (boolean â€” true if the manager must acquire a lock before dispatching this worker); scopes (array of three-column arrays â€” [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] â€” carrying this enforcement's per-enforcement scope-list rules; scope_list_type âˆˆ {allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern}; the EngineeringRulesSchema.json validator enforces this row shape; see Â§4.6); timeout (integer, optional â€” seconds; defaults to manager constant DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 when omitted; the manager passes this value to subprocess.run(..., timeout=N); on timeout the manager kills the worker subprocess and returns EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT (4); the worker does not see this field â€” the timeout is enforced by the parent process; see Â§4.3.2). The four scope-list types are carried only by scopes; there are no separate top-level allowed_exact / allowed_pattern / excluded_exact / excluded_pattern fields on the entry.

requirement.name: Manager class and exit codes
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. Single class. Single main. Constructor signature __init__(hook_name: str). run returns int. The manager module defines the following named exit-code constants and run returns one of them: EXIT_OK = 0 (all matched enforcements passed), EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1 (at least one worker reported violations; commit/push must block), EXIT_MANAGER_ERROR = 2 (manager-level failure: cannot read engineering_rules.json, malformed schema, unknown hook name, or any other pre-dispatch error), EXIT_WORKER_SPAWN_FAILURE = 3 (one or more workers could not be launched: missing executable_path, executable not found, permission denied, OSError on subprocess), EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT = 4 (one or more workers exceeded the configured subprocess timeout), EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR = 5 (a worker exited with a non-0 / non-1 status â€” i.e. anything â‰¥ 3 from a worker is treated as an internal worker failure rather than a violation). Aggregation by precedence (highest wins): 2 > 3 > 5 > 4 > 1 > 0. Manager-level errors trump worker errors trump violations trump success, so the caller can immediately tell whether the issue is in the framework or in the user's code. Worker exit codes follow the same convention for the worker's subset: 0 = clean, 1 = violations, 2 = worker error; any worker exit â‰¥ 3 is promoted by the manager to EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirement.name: Manager load-filter-spawn
requirement.requirement: Manager loads engineering_rules.json read-only, filters enforcement[] by hook, and for each matching enforcement reads executable_path and spawns the worker via subprocess.run([sys.executable, executable_path, enforcement_id], timeout=...). The manager collects each subprocess returncode and aggregates by the TR-2 exit-code precedence.

requirement.name: EnforcementWorker base class
requirement.requirement: EnforcementWorker (abstract base) lives at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/enforcement_worker.py. It owns: __init__(enforcement_id), _load_enforcement, is_in_scope(resource), main (CLI entry that parses enforcement_id, instantiates the subclass, calls run, returns its exit code), violation emission, telemetry emission, and structured error handling. Subclasses implement run and any private helper methods their domain requires.

requirement.name: Violation record shape
requirement.requirement: Violation record shape (emitted by the base class): {enforcement_id, rule_id, resource, message, severity}. severity in {info, warn, error}.

requirement.name: Telemetry envelope
requirement.requirement: Telemetry envelope (emitted by the base class): start record and end record per worker invocation, both carrying enforcement_id, hook, duration_ms, files_scanned, violation_count, exit_code. Format: one JSON object per line to stdout.

requirement.name: Manager-owned mutex
requirement.requirement: When an enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True, the manager MUST acquire a process-safe lock keyed on enforcement_id before invoking subprocess.run, and MUST release the lock after subprocess.run returns (clean, non-zero, or timeout). Default mechanism: advisory file lock. In-process Python locks are forbidden. Workers do not declare a concurrency primitive.

requirement.name: Manager-worker contract
requirement.requirement: Manager and workers MUST NOT import each other's internals. The only contract is enforcement_id (str) in via CLI argv, exit code (int) out via subprocess returncode, and the structured stdout (violation + telemetry) envelope.

requirement.name: Tests location
requirement.requirement: Tests live at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/. The base class ships with its own test suite covering scope evaluation, exit-code semantics, violation shape, telemetry envelope, and the try/except fail-safe. Each new worker ships with at least one happy-path and one violation-path test.

requirement.name: Hook plumbing
requirement.requirement: Hook plumbing..git/hooks/{pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push} each invoke `python <repo-root>/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py --hook <hook>`..claude/settings.json registers the same invocation under SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded with the matching `--hook <hook_name>` flag. A pytest under architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/ MUST verify, for every hook named above: (a) hard assert the wire-up exists when the hook carries at least one enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json; (b) advisory warning when the wire-up is missing and the hook has no enforcement (reserved for future Phase-6 workers). The test runs in the F-002 suite and the hard assertions gate pre-push.

requirement.name: Worker taxonomy
requirement.requirement: Worker taxonomy supported by the framework: file scanning (pre-commit / pre-push), prompt-injection check (UserPromptSubmit â€” returns additionalContext), post-response audit (Stop), log publishing (UserPromptSubmit + Stop -> Kafka), boot orchestration (SessionStart), and mode selection (SessionStart). Each is a concrete subclass of EnforcementWorker, deployed as its own standalone executable.

story.name: Scanning: file enumeration on hooks, SCOPES evaluation, scope precedence
story.description: Per V20 Â§4.5 and Â§4.9. Workers receive resource candidates (staged or about-to-push files for the V1 ScanFilesEnforcementWorker), evaluate each via the base-class is_in_scope walk against the SCOPES rows on the enforcement entry, and dispatch matched check methods. Scope precedence is fixed and lives entirely in the base class.

requirement.name: Scope walk precedence
requirement.requirement: Scope evaluation is fixed-precedence and lives entirely in the base class. For each (resource, function_name) the base class walks the matching rows in self.scopes (filtered by function_name) in this fixed order: excluded_exact, excluded_pattern, allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, then per-check SCOPE_DEFAULT. Subclasses do not override this walk. The default behavior (in scope vs. out of scope when no row matched) is declared per check via the per-method SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute.

requirement.name: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker (worked example, V1) lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_files_enforcement_worker.py. It is a standalone Python script with a main that takes enforcement_id as a CLI argument and exits with a status code. Its run implements two domain checks synchronously, in this order, on every in-scope file: (a) _scan_http(file) â€” the HTTP-vs-HTTPS regex scan ported from preCommitScan.py; (b) _validate_json(file) â€” the JSON schema validation ported from validate_all_json.py. Both run inside the same subprocess. Multi-threading inside run is a documented future enhancement, not V1. requires_lock = false (read-only worker; the manager dispatches without acquiring a lock). ScanFilesEnforcementWorker's scope-list rules live in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field (see Â§4.6); the worker inherits the default _load_scopes from EnforcementWorker, which returns self.entry.get("scopes", []). It does NOT override _load_scopes and contributes no SCOPES class attribute (see Â§4.5 for the mechanism, Â§4.9.1 for the per-method spec, and Â§4.9.2 for the worked-example rows).

requirement.name: Scope rows on enforcement entry
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker scope rules are expressed as a flat three-column list in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field. Each row has the shape [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] where scope_list_type is one of the four canonical terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) and function_name is the name of a check method on the worker (e.g. _scan_http, _validate_json). The EnforcementWorker base class loads the list at worker startup through the virtual _load_scopes method, whose default implementation returns self.entry.get("scopes", []); ScanFilesEnforcementWorker inherits that default and does NOT override it. The base class then resolves function_name to a bound method via getattr(self, row[0]) at startup, so a typo in function_name fails loudly rather than silently dropping a rule. The ordered precedence of the four types is fixed in the base class per TR-5 and is described in narrative form in Â§4.5. The SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute is per-check: False for _scan_http (don't flag a path that no rule matched), True for _validate_json (every governed JSON is in scope unless explicitly excluded). The canonical worked example â€” exactly the rows used by V1 â€” is in Â§4.9.2.

requirement.name: preCommitScan.py JSON retirement
requirement.requirement: preCommitScan.py SHALL drop ".json" from SCAN_EXTENSIONS and \.json$ from HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS once ScanFilesEnforcementWorker is the single source of truth (note: SCAN_EXTENSIONS and HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS are legacy module-level names inside preCommitScan.py â€” the artifact being retired â€” and are not part of the new framework's vocabulary; the new framework uses scopes rows in engineering_rules.json). Once the manager dispatches all enforcement, preCommitScan.py is retired.

requirement.name: Scan must test this content
requirement.requirement: The scan rule Must test for: (a) Font compliance â€” see EPIC-008-F-011-S-003-REQ-B-004 (Scan of all relevant files must test font compliance); (b) JSON Schema validation â€” see EPIC-008-F-002-S-012 (JSON validation: _validate_json check, $schema web-fetch resolver, meta-schema carve-out, in-run cache); (c) HTTPS compliance â€” see EPIC-008-F-002-S-012 (HTTP vs HTTPS: _scan_http check and allowed_pattern URL handling).

story.name: Rule-002 - Boot execution on SessionStart and PostCompact
story.description: On every Claude Code SessionStart hook and on every PostCompact hook (context purge), the boot program replays the most recent conversation utterances from MongoDB and injects the agile_backlog taxonomy. Dispatch is performed by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py per Rule-002 enforcement entries; the boot is no longer wired directly in .claude/settings.json.

requirement.name: Replay 170 most recent utterances from Mongo into SessionStart additionalContext
requirement.requirement: On SessionStart, chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read the 170 most recent utterance documents from MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, trim each document to {actor, content}, order newest-first, and emit them as part of the hook's additionalContext so Claude resumes with recent conversation context. If the MongoDB read fails (connection, auth, or query error), the boot MUST fail open - log the failure to stderr and continue with remaining SessionStart duties without aborting the session.

requirement.name: Inject agile_backlog taxonomy (epic+feature descriptions, story names) into SessionStart additionalContext
requirement.requirement: On SessionStart, chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json and emit the business taxonomy as part of the hook's additionalContext: every epic's id, name, and description; every feature's id, name, and description; every story's id and name. Story descriptions, requirements, and tests MUST NOT be emitted. The output is the operator-facing context shape, not a context-resident @-import.

requirement.name: Read hook_event_name from stdin to branch SessionStart and PostCompact dispatch
requirement.requirement: chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read the Claude Code hook payload JSON from stdin and dispatch on the hook_event_name field. SessionStart and PostCompact MUST each execute the two duties in EPIC-008-F-002-S-007-REQ-T-002 and EPIC-008-F-002-S-007-REQ-T-003 in order. Any other hook_event_name value MUST be a no-op that exits 0. Each branch MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally that calls sys.exit so control always returns to the enforcement manager.

requirement.name: Boot is invoked exclusively through Rule-002 enforcement entries, not direct settings.json wiring
requirement.requirement: chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST NOT appear directly in .claude/settings.json hooks. It is invoked exclusively via Rule-002 enforcement entries (Rule-002-ENF-001 on SessionStart, Rule-002-ENF-002 on PostCompact) dispatched by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. .claude/settings.json registers only the enforcement manager (one entry per hook); the manager loads engineering_rules.json and spawns the matching enforcement workers.

story.description: Catalog entry. Semantic requirements live at EPIC-008-F-013-S-001 (Publisher leg) - REQ-T-001 (UserPromptSubmit publish), REQ-T-002 (Stop publish), REQ-B-001 (sidecar-unreachable fullscreen browser warning). story.name: Rule-003 - Deliberate raises must use ChatHealthyException
story.description: Establishes the foundational rule and the implementation that realizes it. Defines ChatHealthyException in chathealthy-lib, specifies the constructor contract (mode discriminator + message for logging + context dict), mandates the substitution at every existing deliberate-raise site in our authored code, and adds a pre-commit gate that rejects new raises of forbidden built-in exception types in our modules. The first mode the substrate uses is llm_unavailable, introduced by the LLM facade with context {provider, call_site, attempts}. Additional modes (compliance violations, geography insufficient, db unreachable, rate limited, etc.) land as the operator approves their definitions; the substrate accepts them without code change at the catch sites.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyException class definition
requirement.requirement: The chathealthy-lib package MUST define a class ChatHealthyException that inherits from the standard library Exception. The constructor signature is (mode: str, message: str, **context). Message is used for logging, and not for end user communications. Context is a dict; its keys vary by mode. The instance exposes attributes mode (str), message (str), context (dict), and exception (Exception â€” the original wrapped exception, when ChatHealthyException is being raised as a boundary conversion of an external library exception; None when this is an originating raise from our own code). The class lives at a stable import path within the package so every consumer service can import it.

requirement.name: Exhaustive use rule for deliberate raises in our authored code
requirement.requirement: Every deliberate raise of an exception authored in ChatHealthy.ai repository code MUST use ChatHealthyException with an appropriate mode discriminator. Use of built-in Python exception types (ValueError, RuntimeError, AssertionError, TypeError, KeyError) in deliberate raises authored by our code is forbidden. Re-raises of external exceptions (e.g. httpx.RemoteProtocolError, pymongo.errors.*) preserve the original type and the call stack of the original exception, so that logging of the exception becomes the duty of the exception class and not the code that creates the exception.

requirement.name: Boundary conversion rule for external-library exceptions
requirement.requirement: External-library exceptions MAY be converted to ChatHealthyException at defined system boundaries. The LLM facade (EPIC-008-F-002-S-009-REQ-B-007 below) is one such boundary. When such a conversion happens, the exception object MUST log the original exception with full traceback for operator forensic value before raising the new ChatHealthyException, so the original failure is not lost.

requirement.name: Catch-side discrimination on mode
requirement.requirement: Code that catches ChatHealthyException SHOULD discriminate on the mode attribute, not on isinstance against new exception subclasses (there are no subclasses). The mode taxonomy is the design surface for discriminating failure shapes. Catch sites that need to handle several modes use an explicit conditional on exc.mode.

requirement.name: Mode taxonomy lives in the feature's design doc
requirement.requirement: The set of valid modes is documented in the feature's architecture design doc under ChatHealthyLib/architectureAndDesign/. Adding a new mode is a design-doc edit that the operator approves, not a code-only change. Code that raises with an undocumented mode MAY be rejected by a future enforcement gate (out of scope for this story).

requirement.name: Pre-commit gate forbids deliberate raises of built-in types
requirement.requirement: A new engineering rule (Rule-NNN, operator picks the number) MUST gate pre-commit. The worker scans every staged Python file under ChatHealthy.ai's authored directories (sharedServices/, FindCare/, evaluateCare/, Code/, ChatHealthyLib/, architecture/) and rejects any line matching a deliberate raise of ValueError, RuntimeError, AssertionError, KeyError, TypeError. Exempted: re-raises with no expression, test files asserting expected behavior, and external-library calls that we do not author. Any violation found — new or legacy — is rejected. No carve-outs for historical code.

requirement.name: LLM facade boundary defines the first concrete mode llm_unavailable
requirement.requirement: The LLM call facade in chathealthy-lib catches transient HTTP errors (httpx.RemoteProtocolError, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadTimeout, httpx.WriteTimeout, httpx.PoolTimeout) from the underlying pydantic-ai Agent.run call and, after the retry policy is exhausted, raises ChatHealthyException(mode='llm_unavailable', provider=<str>, call_site=<str>, attempts=<int>). UR catches this exception in _handle_utterance and re-dispatches to UM as a manufacture-trigger Request whose manufacture_utterance_reason carries the same context, so UM authors a user-facing message via the existing manufacture pattern. If the manufacture call itself raises ChatHealthyException, that exception propagates to UR's outermost catch and the existing fatal path fires; the operator sees the failure via telemetry and the user sees chFatalError. This three-rung ladder (transient blip covered by retry, sustained-recoverable covered by manufacture dialogue, truly-down covered by fatal) is the substrate.

requirement.name: Exception Management Modes
requirement.requirement: Every catch site that catches a ChatHealthyException MUST classify the caught exception into exactly one of three modes and act accordingly. Mode 1 â€” expected and easily handled (retry, fallback, alternate path): catcher logs at INFO with the if_debug flag set so the record is emitted only when in debug; caller continues via the recovery mechanism; user sees nothing. Mode 2 â€” expected and probably attributable to user error OR to a resource temporarily unavailable: catcher logs at ERROR (always emitted, no debug gate), surfaces an appropriate user-facing message describing the problem, and does NOT return HTTP 503. Mode 3 â€” unhandled, NOT expected (a bug): the safety-net @app.exception_handler returns HTTP 503 to the user and logs the unhandled exception so we can track it down and fix it; Mode 3 is the ONLY case where the user sees an HTTP 503; the architectural goal is for Mode 3 occurrences to be RARE â€” every observed Mode 3 instance MUST become a local catch with Mode 1 or Mode 2 handling. Throw-side rule: when a catch site converts a library exception (httpx, pymongo, etc.) into a ChatHealthyException, that site MUST clean up the underlying resource (close the connection / cursor / file handle, abort the request, release the pool slot, etc.) before raising the ChatHealthyException, so a leaked resource does not produce a delayed second failure (e.g., a 100-second-later timeout from a connection that was never closed).

story.name: Rule-004 - Direct MongoClient instantiation forbidden outside the canonical utility
story.description: ChatHealthyMongoUtilities (lives at ChatHealthyLib/src/chathealthy_lib/mongo_utilities.py) is the canonical entry point for obtaining a MongoClient. Every live service path uses it. Direct MongoClient(...) instantiation outside the utility itself is forbidden and enforced at pre-commit via Rule-004.

requirement.name: Canonical Mongo client provider exists
requirement.requirement: A class named ChatHealthyMongoUtilities MUST exist at ChatHealthyLib/src/chathealthy_lib/mongo_utilities.py and serve as the canonical Mongo client provider for every ChatHealthy.ai service.

requirement.name: Zero-parameter constructor, environment-sourced configuration
requirement.requirement: The constructor takes zero parameters. The utility sources connection coordinates and service identity from runtime environment configuration without caller input.

requirement.name: Process-wide singleton client
requirement.requirement: The utility maintains a process-wide singleton MongoClient. Repeated instantiation of ChatHealthyMongoUtilities returns the same underlying client and connection pool.

requirement.name: getConnection() is the single public method
requirement.requirement: getConnection() is the single public method. It returns the MongoClient. Callers select their own database and collection from the returned client.

requirement.name: Default operation timeout
requirement.requirement: The utility sets timeoutMS on the MongoClient per the CSOT (Client-Side Operation Timeout) policy, with default value 15000ms.

requirement.name: Per-call overrides use pymongo's native context manager
requirement.requirement: Per-call timeout overrides are performed by the calling code using pymongo's native `with pymongo.timeout(seconds):` context manager. The utility does NOT expose a wrapper API for timeout overrides.

requirement.name: Direct MongoClient instantiation forbidden outside the utility
requirement.requirement: Direct MongoClient(...) instantiation in any ChatHealthy.ai-authored Python file is forbidden except within ChatHealthyLib/src/chathealthy_lib/mongo_utilities.py itself.

requirement.name: Logging is governed by uniform application logging
requirement.requirement: The utility's logging surface is governed by EPIC-008-F-011-S-005 (Uniform application logging).

depends_on.reason: Logging surface is governed by the uniform application logging story.

requirement.name: Explicit per-call batch_size override on library find()
requirement.requirement: The ChatHealthyMongoUtilities Mongo wrapper SHALL expose batch_size as an explicit named keyword parameter on its find() method, with default value None. When batch_size is None the library MUST NOT pass any batch_size to pymongo (pymongo default applies). When the caller sets batch_size to an integer, the library MUST forward that integer to pymongo. The library MUST NOT impose a default batch_size for any caller, MUST NOT cache or persist a batch_size across calls, and MUST NOT infer a batch_size from collection size or call history. Choosing to override batch_size is a per-call caller decision. Compliance test: a pytest configures the canonical logging service to DEBUG, calls find() with batch_size set to a known integer, then reads the configured log destination and asserts the captured mongo.find START line includes the batch_size kwarg verbatim. The same pytest also asserts that omitting batch_size results in a START line that does NOT include batch_size in opts.

requirement.name: Mongo utility library has no cluster or workload knowledge
requirement.requirement: The chathealthy_lib mongo utility MUST have zero references to any Mongo cluster facts.

story.name: Rule-005 - Uniform logging discipline
story.description: Every ChatHealthy.ai Python file MUST get its logger from ChatHealthyLoggingService in chathealthy_lib. ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's logging module. logging.basicConfig(), logging.getLogger(), and print() MUST NOT appear in ChatHealthy.ai code. Pre-commit Rule-005 MUST enforce this.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyLoggingService is the only place loggers come from
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyLoggingService MUST exist in chathealthy_lib. Every ChatHealthy.ai Python file MUST get its logger from it.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: logging.basicConfig(), logging.getLogger(), and print() are forbidden in ChatHealthy.ai code
requirement.requirement: logging.basicConfig(), logging.getLogger(), and print() MUST NOT appear in any ChatHealthy.ai Python file except ChatHealthyLoggingService itself. Pre-commit Rule-005 MUST enforce this.

requirement.name: Default log level and destination come from environment variables
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyLoggingService MUST read its default log level and log destination from environment variables. If no environment variable is set, the default level MUST be INFO.

depends_on.reason: ChatHealthyLoggingService uses Python's standard library logging module.

requirement.name: All log messages, including 3rd-party library logs, write to the same log file
requirement.requirement: All log messages from ChatHealthy.ai code AND from other Python libraries (pymongo, openai, httpx, etc.) MUST write to the same log file. ChatHealthyLoggingService MUST route them via handlers configured on the root logger.

Any other file found to contain the term "http:" is a violation and the commit MUST be blocked.

requirement.name: _scan_http scope alignment

requirement.name: Governed JSON validation gate
requirement.requirement: Every file the system treats as governed JSON content MUST validate cleanly against the schema declared in its $schema field. The set of governed JSON files is defined using only the four permitted scope-list terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern). The system MUST NOT trust data from a JSON file that fails schema validation, and the framework MUST treat validation failure as a governance violation. JSON validation is the load-bearing gate that protects the entire governed-data layer from silent drift.

requirement.name: Draft 2020-12, no opt-out
requirement.requirement: Governed JSON content lives under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Each governed JSON file MUST declare its schema URL in a top-level $schema field. JSON parsing uses Python's standard library json module. Schema validation uses the jsonschema package against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Validation failure produces a violation record per TR-6 and contributes to the worker's exit code (EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1). Files identified by the worker's excluded_exact or excluded_pattern lists are skipped silently; files in scope without a $schema field MUST FAIL LOUD. There is no opt-out, and there is no quiet passing of unschemaed JSON content. The JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema URL is the single resolver carve-out, served from a local copy at Website/schemas/standard/json-schema-2020-12-meta.json. All other $schema URLs are resolved by HTTP GET with a 5-second timeout and per-run cache.

requirement.name: Validation uses $schema URL
requirement.requirement: Validation MUST use the schema referenced by the JSON file's $schema URL.

requirement.name: External standards committed

requirement.name: $schema HTTPS resolution + cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-15. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET to the URL the JSON file declared, performed at validation time. A per-run cache deduplicates identical URLs within a single worker invocation. Unreachable URL, non-200, timeout, or non-JSON response body produces a per-file ViolationRecord per TR-6.

requirement.name: External-standard carve-out cache

A standard is eligible for caching when its URL is contractually frozen by the spec maintainer (any change requires a new versioned URL). The framework's runtime serves those URLs from the cached copies. Cached standards remain under the stewardship of their original publisher; the framework's governance applies to content the framework owns.

story.name: Rule-009 - Separation of concerns between React display, plumbing JS/HTML, and Python tools
story.description: Defines the architectural separation enforced by Rule-009. React owns all display content authoring; tool code (Python) owns all persistent-state change and business logic; authored .js files outside the React source tree and authored .html files are plumbing only - they courier opaque content between React and tools, never authoring display, never changing data state, and never carrying business logic. Worker: architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_separation_of_concerns_worker.py.

requirement.name: No display authoring outside React
requirement.requirement: Authored .js files outside the React application source tree (Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/frontend/src/) and authored .html files MUST NOT author display content. Display content authoring includes assignments to innerHTML, outerHTML, textContent, or innerText; programmatic construction of DOM nodes carrying visible text or styles; and emitting template literals containing HTML markup. Couriering an opaque content string handed in via postMessage and assigning it to a named frame is permitted and lives on the enforcement entry's exception list.

requirement.name: No persistent-state change from React
requirement.requirement: The React application MUST NOT change persistent state directly. All persistence changes MUST originate from a /gate call dispatched through ClientRouter. Forbidden in React source: writes to localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, or document.cookie; any fetch, XMLHttpRequest, or navigator.sendBeacon call that does not resolve to the canonical ClientRouter.getStreamedPayloads / ClientRouter.getFullPayload / router:makeCall postMessage path. Approved out-of-band reads (e.g., FindCare's /welcome) live on the enforcement entry's exception list.

requirement.name: No business logic outside tools
requirement.requirement: Authored .js files outside the React source tree and authored .html files MUST NOT carry business logic. Business logic is identified by branching on, or directly reading/writing, domain-vocabulary fields (provider, specialty, NPI, NUCC, clinical_trial, evaluation, user_object) on any payload or DOM value.

requirement.name: Enforcement is deterministic
requirement.requirement: The pre-commit worker that enforces REQ-B-001, REQ-B-002, and REQ-B-003 MUST be deterministic - no LLM call in the pre-commit path. Detection MUST be structural (stdlib html.parser for .html, tree-sitter or equivalent for .js/.ts/.tsx). Where regex on parsed string contents is required, the worker MUST be added to Rule-008's _block_regular_expressions_in_executable_code excluded_exact list per the established pattern.

story.description: On the first user prompt, Claude Code MUST boot the governance singleton and ask the user to select an operating mode (1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot). There MUST be no SessionStart hook. Known bug: BUG-AUTH-001.

requirement.requirement: Each Claude Code session MUST complete a deterministic, non-circumventable boot sequence before any other work. The sequence is: (1) load the governance brain and run compliance checks; (2) at the end of boot, ask the user exactly two questions in order and block all other assistant output until both are answered â€” Q1: mode selection per REQ-010; Q2: orphan triage per REQ-011. The sequence MUST NOT be skippable, paraphrasable, summarizable, or deferrable by Claude Code. Implementation MAY use any hook topology (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop-hook validator, blocking-reply pattern) so long as the user-observable behavior holds: every new session begins with those two questions presented verbatim, in order, with no other assistant output preceding them.
requirement.name: Enforce deterministic boot: governance + 2 mandatory verbatim questions before I

requirement.requirement: After boot completes, Claude Code MUST ask the user to select an operating mode: 1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot. Claude Code MUST NOT proceed until the user has made a selection.
requirement.name: Prompt user to select mode after boot; block execution until selection is made

requirement.requirement: Orphan triage is the second of the two boot questions. After the user answers REQ-010, Claude Code MUST ask a single yes/no question: 'Triage orphan bugs?' If the user answers no, boot completes and normal work begins. If the user answers yes, Claude Code MUST present the orphan bug table and the user chooses how many to triage this boot â€” one, several, or all. Triaging an orphan means assigning it a req_id or closing it. There is no per-orphan defer option and no obligation to triage every orphan; the single yes/no gate governs whether the list is shown at all, and within 'yes' the user drives how many get worked.
requirement.name: Boot question: Ask user 'Triage orphan bugs?' and present table if answered yes

requirement.requirement: Every action taken within this project MUST be governed by any applicable rule found in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json. These engineering rules MUST be in Claude's 1,000,000 token context and MUST be checked before any action for compliance. If an order from a human or a task Claude or an agent of Claude contradicts any rules, Claude CANNOT take that action or follow that order.
requirement.name: Enforce compliance with engineering_rules.json before any action is taken

requirement.requirement: The user MUST NOT be forced to login twice during the boot sequence. A single interactive login event per identity provider is the limit; a second consecutive prompt for the same user to the same provider within one boot is a failure. If the first login produced a valid session or cached credential, the boot sequence MUST reuse that credential rather than re-prompt.
requirement.name: Prevent duplicate login prompts per identity provider during one boot sequence

requirement.requirement: The boot class MUST be a single Python file with __main__ and a chathealthy_devops_boot class. main dispatches to the class by mode (prompt, tool_call, prompt_result, session_end). There is no boot mode â€” boot is triggered by the prompt handler on first call. Every mode handler MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally. The finally block MUST always call sys.exit to return control to Cursor/Claude Code. All modes MUST fail open on exception.

requirement.requirement: Boot MUST only occur once per session. On SessionEnd, the boot flag in.claude/ChatHealthySettings.json MUST be set to FALSE. On a successful boot from within Anthropic's UserPromptSubmit hook, the flag MUST be set to TRUE. Each subsequent call from the hook MUST check the flag to determine whether the session needs to be booted. If ChatHealthySettings.json or the boot flag cannot be found, an error message MUST be output to the user and no boot is attempted. If SessionEnd does not fire (crash, force-quit), the next session's first prompt will hit the error state and inform the user.

SessionEnd is known not to fire on Cursor window-close or auto-compaction; the SessionStart hook (REQ-007) is the primary clearer, and SessionEnd is the secondary clearer for clean exits (/logout, /exit, /clear).
requirement.name: SessionEnd hook clears booted flag in ChatHealthySettings.json, fails open

requirement.requirement: Three context-resident artifacts MUST be loaded into the Claude Code session context at every session start, and MUST be re-injected after any context compaction: (1) brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json â€” active bug register, loaded in full; (2) brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json â€” engineering rules, loaded in full; (3) _oneshots/test_output/backlog_stories.json â€” story-level pruned view of agile_backlog.json covering Epic â†’ Feature â†’ Story only. The story view carries story metadata (story_id, title, description, parent_feature, sprint, size, status, accepted_by, orphan, approval) plus an integer requirement_count per story. It does NOT carry requirement bodies, pytest pointers, realized_by arrays, or any node below story. The full agile_backlog.json (~521K tokens) is NOT context-resident; specific requirement bodies, pytest ids, and realized_by data MUST be fetched from the canonical brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json via Read when Claude needs them. Canonical brain content lives on disk under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ and is never stored anywhere else. The story view is a derived artifact â€” gitignored, regenerated at session start from the canonical source â€” it does not replace the source. A pytest MUST verify: (a) @-imports for the three context-resident artifacts are present in the root CLAUDE.md; (b) every current file under Code/DataPipelines/ matching the listed extensions (minus excluded dirs) has a corresponding @-import; (c) every @-imported file exists and is non-empty; (d) no @-imported path is stale. A git pre-commit hook MUST regenerate the DataPipelines @-import block when any file under Code/DataPipelines/ is added, moved, or deleted; if the block is stale, pre-commit MUST fail. Purpose: these artifacts are the ones Claude is most prone to shortcut-reasoning about â€” grepping instead of reading, guessing instead of checking, proposing duplicates because the original was never loaded. Making the backlog's high-level shape (9 epics / 83 features / 301 stories) context-resident removes the option to grep-and-punt for structure. Requirement bodies remain on-demand because loading the full backlog at ~521K tokens would consume more than half the 1M context window for content that is rarely needed in full. History: agile_backlog.json was attempted in context-residency 2026-04-18 and was replaced with the story-level view the same day. EPIC-008-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-003 (the flat pipe-delimited req_index.txt view) is deprecated in favor of this story-tree view. API source: Claude Code memory docs at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md â€” '@path/to/import' syntax, 'Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch', 'CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length', 'Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session.' Hook-based injection is NOT a viable substitute because per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks cap additionalContext at 10,000 characters with overflow saved to file + preview â€” too small for these artifacts.

requirement.requirement: Per-artifact load confirmation. After each session boot, the diagnostic MUST emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012. Each line MUST cite the full project-relative path of the artifact. Silent success is not permitted. The diagnostic signal may come from the InstructionsLoaded hook log, a direct content canary, or both; the reporting format is one line per artifact regardless of source. requirement.requirement: Load-failure short message. If any context-resident brain artifact fails load verification at session boot (per REQ-012 and REQ-017), the diagnostic MUST output a single short failure line (one line, under 200 characters) that names the failing artifact and classifies the failure as exactly one of four reasons â€” no more, no less: invalid_json | hash_unreadable | not_loaded | hash_mismatch. A long explanation is a violation of this requirement â€” follow-up detail belongs in a separate report, not the verdict line.

requirement.requirement: Load verification procedure. For each context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012, the diagnostic MUST execute exactly four steps in order, short-circuiting on the first failure: (1) validate the file as JSON â€” on failure emit 'invalid_json'; (2) compute sha256 of the file on disk and retain it â€” on I/O or hash failure emit 'hash_unreadable'; (3) confirm the harness loaded the file into context (InstructionsLoaded event fired for that file_path) â€” on absence emit 'not_loaded'; (4) recompute sha256 at the InstructionsLoaded event and compare to the hash from step 2 â€” on inequality emit 'hash_mismatch'. If all four steps pass, emit one 'LOADED' line per REQ-015. These four failure reasons are exhaustive: the diagnostic MUST NOT introduce a fifth category (e.g. timeout, truncation, attention_drift, unknown). Any observed failure that does not map to one of the four reasons is a gap in the procedure, not a new reason. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts â€” REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list.

When no logical parent exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the entry with orphan = true under the nearest ancestor, flag it for human's async review, and proceed with its work.

feature.name: Audit â€” Technical, Business, Regulatory and Corporate Governance
feature.description: This feature encompasses all the audits that must be done to maintain technical and business history, integrity and regulatory and corporate governance.

story.description: A deterministic Python orchestrator dispatches disposable AI workers to analyze git history, brain artifacts, and current code to identify lost capabilities, undocumented changes, and gaps between intent and implementation. The orchestrator is 100% deterministic â€” all state is on disk, all decisions are file-existence checks. AI is used only inside workers for code analysis. Audits MUST NOT create state changes â€” they only maintain their own notes and documents, and produce findings and recommendations. The orchestrator loops until all jobs are complete or a human sets the stop command in the control file.

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST examine every version of every file in the git repository to establish a complete lineage of what was built, changed, and removed.
requirement.name: Audit all file versions for complete git repository lineage

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that the brain documents as intended but that does not exist in the current codebase. The brain is the authoritative source of intent.
requirement.name: Identify capabilities intended by brain but missing from current codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that was built and subsequently lost due to uncontrolled changes, code rollbacks, or data loss.
requirement.name: Audit identifies capabilities lost via uncontrolled change, rollback, or data

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every AI call, system prompt, and LLM integration that existed in any previous version and determine whether it is active, intentionally replaced, or lost.
requirement.name: Audit all past AI calls, prompts, LLMs; flag active, replaced, or lost ones

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST cross-reference all findings against the agile backlog, bugs, design documents, business plan, work log, punch lists, unrealized ideas, and all other brain artifacts to determine whether each loss is documented or undocumented.
requirement.name: Audit cross-checks findings against all artifacts for documented or undocumented

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce findings categorized as: undocumented losses, documented but unplanned recoveries, and intentional replacements. Each finding MUST include evidence from git history or brain artifacts.
requirement.name: Categorize audit findings; each must include git or brain evidence

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce actionable recommendations for each finding, prioritized by user impact, with effort estimates and a proposed recovery approach.
requirement.name: Audit recommendations prioritized by user impact with effort and recovery plan

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST be repeatable. Running the audit again on the same codebase MUST produce the same findings. The audit is idempotent.
requirement.name: Audit must be repeatable and idempotent, yielding same findings on same codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit output MUST be consumable by both humans (readable report) and machines (structured JSON). The CEO is the primary consumer.
requirement.name: Audit output as human-readable report and structured JSON for CEO consumption

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST NOT modify any source code, database records, brain files, or deployed artifacts. It is a read-only operation. Output is limited to the audit directory only.
requirement.name: Audit is read-only, modifies nothing, output limited to audit directory

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST run to completion autonomously without requiring human intervention beyond the initial start command.
requirement.name: Audit runs autonomously to completion after initial start command

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST survive infrastructure failures (crashes, restarts, context loss) and resume from the last completed unit of work.
requirement.name: Audit recovers from failures and resumes from last completed unit of work

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST track and report its own cost (token consumption) as part of its output.
requirement.name: Audit must track and report its own token consumption in its output

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST have numbered findings where the most important findings are at the top with the lowest number and the least important findings have the highest numbers.
requirement.name: Audit findings numbered by importance, highest priority at top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST make recommendations based on the findings of how to address and remediate each finding.
requirement.name: Audit must recommend remediations for each finding

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST describe its methodology at the top of the report.
requirement.name: Audit report must include methodology description at the top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST document its assumptions under methodology and above findings.
requirement.name: Audit documents assumptions under methodology and above findings

requirement.requirement: Each audit finding MUST be supported with evidence of at least one example from both the codebase (which may be that no code exists) and from the brain (a known best practice, a brain artifact reference, or code with file and line ranges).
requirement.name: Audit finding must cite code and brain evidence examples

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST be a pure Python script with no AI dependencies. All decisions MUST be based on file existence checks and JSON parsing. No LLM calls in the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Pure Python orchestrator with file checks, JSON parsing, no AI or LLM calls

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST loop continuously until all jobs are complete or a human sets the command to stop in the control file. No other mechanism may stop the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Orchestrator loops until all jobs finish or control file stop command is set

requirement.requirement: All orchestrator state MUST be persisted to disk in a control file (control.json). The orchestrator MUST NOT depend on Claude Code context or conversation memory for any decision.
requirement.name: Persist orchestrator state to control.json; no reliance on memory for decisions

requirement.requirement: Each job MUST write a checkpoint file to disk upon completion. If the orchestrator restarts after a crash, it MUST skip completed jobs by checking for existing checkpoint files.
requirement.name: Write checkpoint files on job completion; skip completed jobs after restart

requirement.requirement: AI workers MUST be spawned as disposable agents with no prior context. Each worker receives a self-contained prompt from a file and writes its output to a checkpoint file. Workers have no knowledge of the orchestrator or other workers.
requirement.name: Spawn disposable AI workers with isolated, self-contained prompts and outputs

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST record token usage and duration from each worker in the control file. Total token spend MUST be visible to the human at all times via the control file.
requirement.name: Record per-worker token usage/duration; show total spend in control file

requirement.requirement: All worker output MUST use structured JSON with predefined schemas. No free-form text output. Every finding MUST include evidence (commit hash, file path, or brain file reference).
requirement.name: Worker output uses structured JSON schemas with evidence for every finding

story.name: Uniform application logging
story.description: App-wide rules for runtime logging â€” uniform logging surface, framework choice, environment-driven configuration. Tool subclasses inherit logging from the base class; no per-tool ad-hoc logging or third-party logger calls.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyTool base class implements uniform tool-invocation logging via Python's stdlib logging
requirement.requirement: The ChatHealthyTool base class MUST be the sole logging surface for every tool invocation. Every concrete subclass is logged uniformly by the base class â€” no concrete tool implements its own logging path, and no concrete tool emits print(), ad-hoc file writes, or third-party logger calls inside the dispatch chain. The base class MUST use Python's standard library logging module; logger configuration MUST be via logging.config.dictConfig so handlers, formatters, and per-environment behavior are declarative. Log messages MUST be suppressible by level via environment variable â€” the operator sets LOG_LEVEL (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL) in the runtime environment, and the logger MUST respect that threshold and drop lower-priority messages. The logger MUST support writing to both stdout and stderr (configurable per level â€” e.g., errors to stderr, normal logs to stdout).
