feature.name: Manage REPO promotions. Build and deployments
feature.description: This feature specifies how ChatHealthy.ai governs code commits, promotions, builds, and deployments.

story.name: Commit
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's commit management and governance. How code enters the repository: every commit is explicitly authorized by the operator at the moment it fires, lands on the dev branch and no other, and passes every engineering-rule scan across the whole repository before it is created. A commit that fails any scan is not made.

requirement.name: Every committed file is governed by the rule manager
requirement.requirement: There MUST be an engineering rule enforcing that any file committed to the ChatHealthy.ai repository is subject to governance by ChatHealthy's rule manager. No file reaches the repository without having been examined by the rule manager, and no file is exempt from examination except by an entry on a rule's exclusion list in engineering_rules.json.

story.name: Promote
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's promotion management and governance. How a git baseline is established and advanced through the environment chain: a promote captures the entire working tree at one commit -- nothing stashed, excluded or hidden -- and advances only along the adjacent pairs local to dev, dev to qa, qa to prod, leaving the destination byte-identical to the source.

requirement.name: A promoted tree matches the tree it was promoted from
requirement.requirement: Each promote MUST result in the destination holding a tree identical to the tree of the source it was promoted from. For local to dev the source is the operator's working tree; for dev to qa it is the dev branch tip; for qa to prod it is the qa branch tip. A promote that cannot establish that the two trees are identical MUST fail and MUST NOT advance the destination.

requirement.name: The promote chain
requirement.requirement: Local files promote to dev, dev promotes to qa, and qa promotes to production on the main branch.

requirement.name: No promotion outside the chain
requirement.requirement: Any promotion that is not one of the three pairs in the chain MUST be refused. This includes skipping an environment, promoting in reverse, and promoting an environment to itself.

requirement.name: No file may remain stashed when promoting
requirement.requirement: When promoting, no file may remain stashed. Any stash present MUST be applied into the working tree so the promote carries it; the promote does not proceed while work is parked in a stash.

requirement.name: One uncommittable file fails the whole promotion
requirement.requirement: If any file cannot be committed, the entire promotion MUST fail. A promote is all of the tree or none of it; no partial promotion is produced, and the destination is not advanced.

story.name: Build
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's build management and governance. How source becomes a deployable package: a build reads the working tree for local and origin of the environment's branch for dev, qa and prod, and writes one directory per target per package. The operator names the targets and the packages; there is no build-everything shortcut.

requirement.name: Build data lives entirely in deployment_architecture.json
requirement.requirement: Build data MUST be 100% contained in deployment_architecture.json, and that file MUST have a strict schema. No build fact is held anywhere else -- not in build scripts, not in the build output, not in a second copy of the manifest. The schema MUST forbid undeclared properties, so a fact the schema does not describe cannot be introduced without the schema being changed first.

story.name: Deploy
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's deployment management and governance. How a built package reaches its destination: a deploy reads only the build output, never source, and installs each named package to the target that declares it. The running target reports which build it carries, and the deploy verifies that rather than asserting it.

story.name: Deployment architecture artifact
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's deployment-facts artifact. The artifact deployment_architecture.json contains all of ChatHealthy's deployment facts: every target, every package, every file, every environment binding, every secret and variable declaration, and every identity and role grant. A deployment fact held anywhere else does not exist.

feature.name: Conversation Archive
feature.description: Every operator utterance and every Claude response is recorded as business data in the conversation archive. Capture never delays the interaction and never loses an utterance because something downstream is unavailable, except as an extreme defence. Credentials, secrets and offensive language are removed before anything is archived. Content that never reaches the archive is not kept indefinitely, and the archive is re-examined as knowledge of credentials grows. Every utterance is classified so the archive can be reasoned about. The document shape is governed by https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyDevOpsUtteranceSchema.json

story.name: Capture utterances
story.description: Every operator utterance and every Claude response is captured and lands in the conversation archive, verbatim, correctly attributed, and carrying the time it was made. Capture must never make the operator wait and must never lose an utterance because something downstream is unavailable. Credentials must not reach the archive.

requirement.name: Operator is told when capture fails
requirement.requirement: If an utterance cannot be captured, the operator MUST be shown an unmistakable full-screen warning stating that the utterance was NOT recorded. Capture failure MUST NOT be silent.

requirement.name: Every utterance is recorded
requirement.requirement: Every operator utterance and every Claude response MUST be recorded in the conversation archive.

requirement.name: Capture does not delay the operator
requirement.requirement: Capturing an utterance MUST NOT delay the interaction. No work depending on a remote service may occur before the turn completes.

requirement.name: No utterance is lost while the archive is unreachable
requirement.requirement: No utterance MUST be lost while the conversation archive is unreachable. Captured content MUST be retained until the archive confirms it has been stored, except as an extreme defensive measure to protect disk space or other resources.

requirement.name: No credential, secret or offensive language is stored
requirement.requirement: No credential, secret or offensive language CAN be stored in the conversation archive.

requirement.name: Utterances are recorded verbatim
requirement.requirement: An utterance MUST be recorded exactly as it was made. It MUST NOT be summarised, paraphrased, answered, or replaced by any other text. Only the removal of a credential, secret or item of offensive language may alter it.

requirement.name: Utterances are correctly attributed
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST be attributed to the party that made it. An utterance MUST NOT be attributed to the wrong party.

requirement.name: Utterances carry the time they were made
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST carry the time the utterance was made, which MUST be distinguishable from the time it reached the archive.

requirement.name: Concurrent utterances are all recorded
requirement.requirement: Utterances made concurrently MUST all be recorded. No utterance may be lost, overwritten, or merged with another because two occurred at the same moment.

requirement.name: A removed credential is identified
requirement.requirement: Where a credential is removed from an utterance, the archive MUST identify which credential was removed by stipulating the key of the key/value pair associated with the credential or secret.

requirement.name: Offensive language is redacted
requirement.requirement: When the human operator swears, the curse word or words MUST be replaced with the phrase 'Expletive redacted'.

requirement.name: Every utterance carries the speaker role
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST carry the speaker's part in the exchange, which MUST be distinct from the identity of the speaker.

requirement.name: Every human utterance identifies the person
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance made by a human MUST identify that person. The archive MUST support more than one person.

requirement.name: The time an utterance reached the archive is recorded
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST carry the time it reached the archive, so that archiving latency is measurable.

story.name: Purge
story.description: Captured content that never reaches the archive is not kept indefinitely, its loss is visible, and the archive is re-examined against current knowledge of credentials so that a secret recorded before it was known does not remain.

requirement.name: Unarchived content is deleted after 24 hours
requirement.requirement: Captured content that has not reached the conversation archive within 24 hours MUST be deleted.

requirement.name: Archive is re-scrubbed against current credential knowledge
requirement.requirement: The conversation archive MUST be re-scrubbed against current knowledge of credentials, so that a credential recorded before it was known is removed once it is known.

requirement.name: Content still eligible for archiving is not deleted
requirement.requirement: Captured content that has not yet reached its deletion age MUST NOT be deleted, however many attempts to archive it have failed.

requirement.name: Deletion is recorded
requirement.requirement: When captured content is deleted before reaching the archive, the loss MUST be recorded so that it is known to have occurred and how much was lost.

story.name: Categorize
story.description: All utterances must be categorized with metadata.

requirement.name: Each utterance carries an orderable time
requirement.requirement: Each utterance MUST carry the time it was made in a form the database can index and order chronologically, so that ordering is correct across daylight-saving transitions.

requirement.name: Each utterance carries a human-readable time
requirement.requirement: Each utterance MUST carry its time rendered for reading, in Pacific time on a 12-hour clock. This rendering MUST NOT be used for ordering.

requirement.name: Each utterance speaker is identified
requirement.requirement: Each utterance is from some human user who MUST be identified, or from Claude Code.

requirement.name: Tone is classified
requirement.requirement: Every utterance MUST be classified by tone, using a value from the approved enumeration. No utterance MAY remain without a tone.

requirement.name: Utterance class is classified
requirement.requirement: Every utterance MUST be classified by what it was doing, using a value from the approved enumeration. No utterance MAY remain without an utterance class.

requirement.name: Classification values come from a normative schema
requirement.requirement: The permitted values for tone and utterance class MUST be defined in a normative JSON schema. A classification MUST NOT use a value absent from that schema.

requirement.name: The archive conforms to its schema
requirement.requirement: Every record in the conversation archive MUST validate against the normative schema that governs it.

feature.name: ChatHealthy PKI Certificate Management
feature.description: PKI certificate authority and lifecycle management for ChatHealthy.ai. Owns X.509 certificate issuance, key generation, subject naming, validity periods, storage/retrieval from Azure Key Vault, certificate tracking, and revocation handling. Integrates with identity and authentication subsystems to provide mTLS and mutual authentication infrastructure.

story.name: Certificate Management (umbrella story)
story.description: Umbrella story defining the complete certificate management lifecycle. Establishes the contract that all certificate operations MUST flow through this feature. Covers the decision tree for when to issue, renew, revoke, and retire certificates. Defines the canonical certificate naming authority and the versioning scheme for certificate generations. Establishes the audit trail requirements for all certificate lifecycle events.

story.name: Certificate Issuance - issue X.509 certs for services/clients
story.description: On-demand X.509 certificate issuance for ChatHealthy services, clients, and components. The issuance path accepts a certificate request (CSR or parameters), validates the request against policy (subject name, validity period, key usage), and returns a signed certificate and intermediate chain. Requests originate from service bootstrap (at deploy time), operator direct invocation, or automated renewal triggers. All issued certificates are tracked in the certificate registry.

story.name: Key Generation - generate RSA keypairs
story.description: RSA keypair generation as a prerequisite to certificate issuance. Generates 2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA keypairs depending on security posture requirements per environment. Private keys are generated in-memory, never written to disk in unencrypted form, and immediately enrolled with their paired certificate into the vault. Key generation is deterministic per environment and subject name to enable reproducibility.

story.name: Subject Naming - define how cert CNs are structured
story.description: Certificate subject naming policy. Defines the canonical structure for certificate common names (CNs), subject alternative names (SANs), and issuer names. CNs follow the pattern: <service-id>.<environment>.chathealthy.internal (e.g., findcare-backend.dev.chathealthy.internal). SANs include both DNS and IP forms for multi-homed services. Issuer CN follows: ChatHealthy CA <generation> <environment> (e.g., ChatHealthy CA 1 dev). Naming scheme is immutable once deployed; any change requires a new CA generation.

story.name: Validity Periods - 1 year validity
story.description: Certificate validity periods default to 1 year from issuance. All issued certificates MUST have NotBefore = issuance time and NotAfter = issuance time + 365 days. Certificates approaching expiration (within 30 days) trigger automated renewal via a scheduled job. Manual early renewal is operator-callable. Validity period is immutable once issued; certificates cannot be extended in place.

story.name: Vault Integration - store/retrieve certs from Key Vault
story.description: Azure Key Vault integration for certificate and private key storage. Issued certificates and their private keys are stored in Key Vault with metadata tagging (service_id, environment, generation, issuer_thumbprint). Retrieval is role-gated: only services with the appropriate RBAC role can retrieve their own certificate and key material. All vault operations are logged to the audit trail. Key Vault certificate versions are maintained automatically by Azure; ChatHealthy tracks generation IDs independently for cross-environment promotion.

story.name: Certificate Tracking - track all certificates
story.description: Certificate registry maintained in MongoDB collection ProprietaryData.CertificateRegistry. Every issued certificate is registered with: subject CN, SANs, issuer CN, thumbprint (SHA-1), thumbprint (SHA-256), public key hash, NotBefore, NotAfter, serial number, service_id, environment, generation, CA version, vault location, issuance timestamp, renewal trigger timestamp (if auto-renewed), revocation status. Registry is append-only: updates are new documents, never mutations. Queries against the registry provide the single source of truth for 'which certificates are live' and 'which are approaching expiration'. Registry is auditable and immutable by design.

story.name: Revocation - handle certificate revocation
story.description: Certificate revocation handling for compromised or obsolete certificates. Revocation is initiated by operator command and takes effect immediately: the certificate record in the registry is marked revoked, Key Vault secret is retired (no longer retrievable), and all downstream systems are notified via an audit event. Services holding a revoked certificate MUST detect the revocation on their next authentication check (via certificate pinning validation) and must not accept the certificate for further TLS handshakes. No CRL or OCSP responder is required; revocation state is determined by querying the registry at authentication time.

epic.name: Pipelines
epic.description: This epic defines all the requirements for ChatHealthy's data pipelines, which do data ETL and data quality management, and data enrichment. All of the code lives and executes in Azure and writes to the ChatHealthyDataPipelines cluster.

feature.name: Data Pipeline Infrastructure Requirements
feature.description: This feature specifies the requirements for ChatHealthy's data pipeline infrastructure. The purpose of the feature is to specify the common requirements allowing for data pipelines to be executed in the most possible cost effective manner, with robust reliability and observability.

story.name: A reaper component MUST manage the Pipeline Cluster's uptime
story.description: The pipeline cluster must not be running when nothing needs it.

requirement.name: A Reaper component external to any pipeline runs regularly
requirement.requirement: A component named Reaper MUST exist, MUST be external to every pipeline, and MUST run on a regular basis and at least once per hour, to realize these requirements and so guard against a failure in a pipeline job or an expired reservation made by an agent on behalf of itself or of a human user.

requirement.name: The reaper corrects pipeline job metadata a failed job left wrong
requirement.requirement: When a pipeline job fails to leave its own metadata true, the Reaper MUST correct it, so that no job is recorded in a non-terminal state while it is not running and no lock or reservation is held on behalf of a job that is not running.

requirement.name: An incomplete metadata correction says so
requirement.requirement: When the Reaper cannot complete a correction pass, the pipeline job metadata MUST record that the pass was incomplete and what it did not reach, and MUST be distinguishable from a pass that completed having found nothing to correct.

feature.name: Data Migration
feature.description: This feature specifies the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's migration of published data from the pipeline cluster to the front-end cluster. A migration moves collections from ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData to ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData. A collection arrives under the name it left with. Nothing is transformed in transit. Migration is the only path by which data reaches the front-end cluster. It is separate from the pipeline that produced the data, and runs only when a human releases it.

story.name: Data Migration
story.description: This story specifies the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's migration of published data from the pipeline cluster to the front-end cluster. A migration moves collections from ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData to ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData. A collection arrives under the name it left with. Nothing is transformed in transit. Migration is the only path by which data reaches the front-end cluster. It is separate from the pipeline that produced the data, and runs only when a human releases it.

requirement.name: A migrated collection keeps its name
requirement.requirement: Every collection present in ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData as the result of a migration carries the same name it had in ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData.

requirement.name: Migration is the only way data reaches the front-end cluster
requirement.requirement: No process other than a migration writes to ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData.

requirement.name: A migration runs only after a human releases it
requirement.requirement: Every migration that has run is preceded by a recorded human sign-off for the data it moved.

requirement.name: A migration never alters or removes what is already there
requirement.requirement: No migration changes or removes any document, collection or index that existed before it ran.

requirement.name: A collection that already exists at the destination stops the migration
requirement.requirement: A migration that finds its target collection already present in ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData MUST fail, MUST raise, and MUST log the collection it found. It MUST NOT write.

requirement.name: Every collection is reached through an instance of the one class that realizes this story
requirement.requirement: One class realizes this story. Every collection the migration touches is reached through an instance of that class, one instance per collection. No collection handle is obtained any other way.

requirement.name: The class constructor takes the collection name and nothing else
requirement.requirement: The constructor of the class that realizes this story accepts exactly one argument, the collection name.

requirement.name: The collection name is the only value assigned to the class from outside it
requirement.requirement: No variable on the class that realizes this story is assigned externally other than the collection name.

requirement.name: One file performs the migration
requirement.requirement: Exactly one file in the repository performs migration, and no other file does any part of it.

requirement.name: An engineering rule guarantees the code meets this story
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule parses the migration file with an LLM and guarantees that every requirement of this story is enforced by the code. A file that does not satisfy every requirement is not committed.

requirement.name: Zero trust - the migration's identities exist and are constrained to this story alone
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy's zero-trust infrastructure creates a database user holding only the role this story requires, and an Azure identity holding only the entitlements this story requires. Neither carries any grant beyond what the migration performs.
